question.text: Which of the following is NOT a permissible legal structure for an AIF seeking registration under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012?

answer.text: Company formed under the Companies Act, 2013
Trust formed under a Trust Deed, registered under the Registration Act, 1908
Limited Liability Partnership under the LLP Act, 2008
Sole Proprietorship registered under the Shops & Establishments Act

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI (AIF) Regulations permit four legal structures: (i) Company under Companies Act, 2013, (ii) Trust registered under Registration Act, 1908, (iii) LLP under LLP Act, 2008, and (iv) Body Corporate established under Central/State Legislature. A sole proprietorship is NOT a permitted structure as it lacks separate legal personality. The Trap: This appears in the PDF's Sample Question. Proprietorship can ACCREDIT as an investor (per AI framework) but cannot itself be an AIF legal structure. Candidates often confuse investor-side structure with fund-side structure. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests this directly. Distinct from Mutual Fund legal structure (Trust under SEBI MF Regs). REIT/InvIT have their own Trust structures. PMS (XXI-B) is not pooled — portfolio manager is a company, not a pool.
